stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Move the sliders $N_1$, $N_2$, and $U_1$ to explore the ideal transformer. The ratio $m = N_2/N_1$ sets everything: $U_2 = m \cdot U_1$ and $I_1 = m \cdot I_2$. Witness one step-up configuration ($m > 1$) AND one step-down ($m < 1$).
stages.concept: An ideal transformer transfers all primary power to the secondary through magnetic coupling in the iron core: $U_2/U_1 = N_2/N_1 = I_1/I_2$. Both windings share the same frequency and are in phase.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit each target secondary voltage $U_2$ by adjusting the number of secondary turns $N_2$. $N_1$ and $U_1$ are given. The live readout confirms when you land within $\pm 5\%$ of the target.
stages.concept: To reach a target $U_2$ from a fixed $U_1$, choose $N_2 = N_1 \cdot (U_2/U_1)$. Direct rearrangement of the transformer ratio.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The secondary readouts are hidden. You are given $U_1$, $N_1$, and a target $U_2$. Compute the required $N_2$ on paper, then type it in and submit. Three scenarios in a row, three attempts each.
stages.concept: From $U_2/U_1 = N_2/N_1$, isolate $N_2 = N_1 \cdot U_2/U_1$. Work it out first — the sim will only tell you right or wrong after you commit.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider; witness a step-up and a step-down configuration
labels.tip2: isolate N₂ from the ratio, then dial the slider until U₂ hits the target
labels.tip3: compute N₂ on paper first — submit only when you're sure
labels.peek_tip: Ideal transformer: U₂/U₁ = N₂/N₁. Isolate N₂ from the target U₂ and given U₁, N₁.

1.1: Grab any slider and watch the secondary voltmeter respond.
1.2: When $N_2 > N_1$ the transformer is step-up; when $N_2 < N_1$ it is step-down. Try both.
1.3: Also move $U_1$ across at least two distinct values so you see $U_2$ scale linearly with the primary voltage.

2.1: For a target $U_2$, the required ratio is $m = U_2/U_1$.
2.2: Then $N_2 = m \cdot N_1$. Move the $N_2$ slider until the live $U_2$ readout lands on the target.
2.3: Tolerance is $\pm 5\%$. If the target is 110 V and U₁ is 220 V with N₁ = 1000, then N₂ = 500.

3.1: Write down the given $U_1$, $N_1$, and target $U_2$ on paper first.
3.2: Apply $N_2 = N_1 \cdot (U_2/U_1)$. Plug in the three numbers and simplify.
